answers.gloss: A flux-managed vertex in a per-tier network.
answers.example: ROADM R1 in the zeta tier.
answers.relations: It is part of b09 (flux-fabric); b02 cap-points, b04 conduit-cap-points, b07 carriage-grids, and b10 conduit circuit endpoints may be located on it, while b08 spans run between such vertices.

answers.gloss: A cap point at which a flux-span terminates on a vertex.
answers.example: The R1 cap point facing R2.
answers.relations: It is on b01 and terminates b08. Unlike b04, it is a span termination rather than the originating or terminating head of an end-to-end conduit.

answers.gloss: The backing relationship by which a cap point is supported by a server-tier cap point.
answers.example: A zeta-tier cap point backed by an optical-tier cap point at R1.
answers.relations: It supports b02 across tier boundaries. It denotes adaptation/backing between client- and server-tier cap points, not an ordinary link or span.

answers.gloss: The point at which a flux-conduit originates or terminates—its run head.
answers.example: The head of the A1–A3 conduit at A1.
answers.relations: It lies on b01 and originates or terminates b05. It differs from b02 because b04 bounds an end-to-end conduit, whereas b02 terminates a network span.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end traffic-engineered conduit that realizes an offer.
answers.example: The A1–A3 grd2 conduit.
answers.relations: It runs from/to b04 conduit-cap-points, traverses b09, is labeled by b06, and includes b10 circuit endpoints. It denotes the realized end-to-end conduit/service, not merely a physical span.

answers.gloss: A zeta-tier label expressing carrier-slot multiplexing structure.
answers.example: The carrier slots carrying grd2 within a crr4.
answers.relations: It labels b05 and identifies its carrier-slot allocation or multiplexing position, represented as xs/xpn.

answers.gloss: The grid of permitted internal carriage within a vertex.
answers.example: The permitted carriage grid on R2.
answers.relations: It is located on b01 and captures which internal carriage or cross-switching is permitted at that vertex.

answers.gloss: A flux-managed span between vertices in a tier network.
answers.example: The R1–R2 flux-span.
answers.relations: It runs between b01 vertices, is terminated by b02 cap-points, and is contained in b09.

answers.gloss: A per-tier flux-managed network.
answers.example: The zeta-tier network.
answers.relations: It contains b01 vertices and b08 spans; b05 conduits are realized over it.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a conduit circuit within a vertex.
answers.example: The circuit endpoint for the A1–A3 conduit on R1.
answers.relations: It is located on b01 and is part of b05. It is specifically an endpoint of the conduit’s circuit within a node, distinct from the conduit run head b04.

answers.gloss: A forwarding vertex in the single multi-tier fabric, not intrinsically a separate node scoped to one tier-specific network.
answers.example: ROADM R1.
answers.relations: It is part of a09. Span-cap-points a02, offer-gateway-points a04, shifting-spans a03, vertex-gate-sets a07, and circuit endpoints a10 may be associated with it; a08 spans run between vertices.

answers.gloss: An edge point owned by a vertex at which a topological span terminates.
answers.example: The R1 edge point toward R2, hep-R1-R2.
answers.relations: It is on a01 and terminates a08. It is a span termination, unlike a04, which is an external client-offer access point.

answers.gloss: A span-like adaptation object expressing bridging between layers at a vertex.
answers.example: The crr4/grd2 bridging at R1.
answers.relations: It is at a01 and adapts a06. Although related in purpose to cross-tier backing, it is modeled as a bridging span tied to a stream qualifier, rather than specifically as a backing relationship between two cap-points.

answers.gloss: A gateway point where an external client offer accesses the network.
answers.example: The grd2 client hand-off at A1, acp-A1-grd.
answers.relations: It is on a01 and provides access to a05. It is not a span termination like a02, nor is it defined as the run head of an internally realized conduit.

answers.gloss: An offered end-to-end carriage service across the network.
answers.example: The A1–A3 grd2 carriage offer, co-a1a3-grd2.
answers.relations: It uses a04 access points, is realized by a10 circuit endpoints, is qualified by a06, and runs over a09. It denotes the offer itself rather than a distinct traffic-engineered conduit that realizes an offer.

answers.gloss: A qualifier expressing the multiplexing and tier structure of a signal.
answers.example: grd2 mapped into a crr4 server.
answers.relations: It qualifies a05 and is the adaptation target of a03. It expresses the client/server multiplexing structure; it is not limited by definition to a concrete carrier-slot allocation, though such allocation may be part of that structure.

answers.gloss: The set of constraints defining which ports may be cross-switched within a vertex.
answers.example: The permitted cross-switches on R2.
answers.relations: It is located on a01 and governs permitted internal switching or carriage there.

answers.gloss: A topological span between two vertices.
answers.example: The R1–R2 span, span-R1-R2.
answers.relations: It runs between a01 vertices, is terminated by a02 span-cap-points, and is contained in a09.

answers.gloss: The single multi-tier fabric describing the whole forwarding realm.
answers.example: The zeta-over-optical fabric.
answers.relations: It contains a01 vertices and a08 spans, and a05 carriage offers operate over it. Unlike a per-tier network, it encompasses the tiers together in one fabric.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a circuit within a vertex.
answers.example: The circuit endpoint for the A1–A3 offer on R1, cxp-a1a3-R1.
answers.relations: It is on a01 and part of a05's realization. It is an internal circuit endpoint, distinct from a04, which is the external client-offer gateway.

proposals.rationale: Both denote a vertex-owned termination point for a topological span, with matching R1-toward-R2 examples and relations to the node and span.

Both express the multiplexing placement of grd2 within a crr4 carrier/server structure. b06 appears somewhat narrower because it emphasizes concrete carrier-slot allocation, while a06 is a general tier-and-stream qualifier.
Both denote the permitted internal carriage or cross-switch constraints at a vertex.
Both denote a span between vertices terminated by span cap-points. B scopes its span to a per-tier fabric, but the underlying span concept and endpoint relations match.
Both denote an endpoint of an end-to-end service or conduit circuit within a vertex, distinct from an external or run-head access point.

ratifications.reason: Both denote a cap or edge point on a vertex that terminates a topological span; their examples and core relations coincide.

b06 specifically denotes a zeta carrier-slot label identifying concrete multiplexing allocation on a conduit. a06 is a broader signal qualifier covering client/server tier and multiplexing structure, so they are related but not equivalent.
Both denote the constraints or grid of permitted internal carriage and cross-switching at a vertex.

b08 is intrinsically a flux-managed span within one tier-specific network, whereas a08 belongs to A's single multi-tier fabric and is not intrinsically scoped to a per-tier network. The structural scope is part of b08's meaning.
Both denote an internal endpoint of an end-to-end circuit within a vertex, distinct from an external gateway or conduit run head.
